text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Thursday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- New finance minister, 34-year-old economist Algirdas Shemeta, entered the cabinet. His most recent job was as head of the securities comission.

- France suggested to establish "special relations" between NATO and Baltic countries to dispel their worries concerning the adoption of new members to the Alliance. NATO diplomats say that the Baltic states most probably will not be adopted to NATO during the first stage of its expansion.

- The regional elections comission excluded the name of the well known U.S. enviroment protection expert Valdas Adamkus from the list of candidates to participate in the municipality elections on March 23 on the grounds that he has not dropped his U.S. citizenship.
- A rising U.S. dollar against the mark has also increased the value of the litas. The present low mark rate agaist the litas annoys exporters but experts say there is nothing to fear.

- The director of human resourses at Ignalina power plant Rimantas Kumpis was sacked after accusations he accepted employees without the necessary recomendations, some of them even having a history of mental problems.
- Various companies and organisations received charity worth $57 million in 1996.
- Bloc trades dominated the stock exchange.
- Vilnius Bank will issue a two month 40 million litas credit to the social insurance and pension fund with an 11 percent annual interest rate to pay pensions.
- There were 6,432 people registered as candidate to 1,484 mandates for the local elections on March 23.
